summary: EfficientNet-B5 Phase 1 on full (uncropped) images at 456px. lr=1.5e-4, wd=0.01, bs=16, 30 epochs. Run completed cleanly on a second machine (no OOM). Best overall accuracy 78.65% at epoch 29. This is the control run against b5_crop_v1/phase1 (79.87% @ ep30) — isolates the contribution of crop preprocessing vs. the B5 backbone alone. Crops add +1.22pp overall but the picture is nuanced per-task: crops help facade-dependent tasks but hurt setting detection which relies on street context.

vs_b5_crop_v1_phase1.overall: -1.22pp (78.65% vs 79.87%). Crops give a modest but consistent overall improvement.
vs_b5_crop_v1_phase1.stories: -3.94pp (72.55% vs 76.49%). Crops help by framing the facade tightly — eave line and storey count become clearer.
vs_b5_crop_v1_phase1.roof_type: -1.92pp (65.30% vs 67.22%). Crops include the roofline so the gain is from resolution/capacity, not context removal.
vs_b5_crop_v1_phase1.primary_cladding: -3.76pp (73.70% vs 77.46%). Crops remove confounding sky and street texture that was hurting cladding classification.
vs_b5_crop_v1_phase1.chimney_present: +0.06pp (94.96% vs 94.90%). Binary saturated task — no meaningful difference.
vs_b5_crop_v1_phase1.setting_exact: +6.58pp (77.54% vs 70.96%). Full images are meaningfully better for setting. Setting (corner, mid-block, setback) depends on street context and lot geometry — both of which crops discard.

comparison.vs_resnet50_v1_phase1: +6.51pp overall (78.65% vs 72.14%). B5 backbone at 456px on full images already dominates ResNet50/224px even without crops.
comparison.crop_vs_full_conclusion: Crops are beneficial overall but introduce a tradeoff: +3-4pp on facade tasks, -6.6pp on setting. If setting accuracy matters, a two-branch or multi-scale approach may be needed. For the primary objective (architectural style, stories, cladding), crops win.

learnings: B5/full vs B5/crops: crops are a net positive (+1.22pp) but the setting regression (-6.58pp) is large enough to matter if setting is a primary target.

Setting is uniquely sensitive to context: it is the only task where full images outperform crops. This is expected — corner vs. mid-block vs. setback is determined by the building's relationship to the street, not its facade texture.
No OOM at bs=16 on this machine (likely ≥16GB unified memory). The MPS OOM seen in b5_crop_v1 was machine-specific.

Gradual val_loss divergence: train_loss reached ~0.002 (fully overfit) while val_loss climbed to ~0.35+. Same pattern as b5_crop_v1 — this is inherent to the dataset size (~7,135 buildings) vs. B5 capacity. Early stopping would not have helped materially given the accuracy plateau in later epochs.
Best at ep29, not ep30 — minor noise at the tail, no meaningful difference. The model essentially plateaued from ep25 onward.
next_steps: Run b5_full_v1/phase2 to compare phase2 arch_style accuracy on full images vs. crops (crops may hurt arch_style if street context is informative).
Consider a hybrid: use crops for stories/cladding heads, full images for setting head — requires architectural change (two encoders or multi-scale input).
Given setting is better with full images, any production model should either use full images or add a secondary branch for setting.
